description: Actual before/after proof-pass timings and emitted code sizes. Original run and justified alternating-process follow-up both retained.

followup.description: Bounded follow-up for unresolved short-kernel timing differences. Same already-built binaries, five alternating process blocks, one warmup and five samples per process; no rebuilding or optimization changes.
followup.reason: Initial O2 bounded fixture was slower with proof despite zero remaining checks in both variants; initial O0 baseline/off also differed.
limits: Not affinity/power/thermal controlled. Do not select only favorable samples or erase the initial run.
Observed differences alone establish neither proof-caused speedup nor regression.
Raw-emission wall time includes process creation, frontend, imported modules, analysis, and text output; it is not isolated compile CPU time.
analysis_nanoseconds is the pass's internal reported duration; disabled mode has no comparable pass work.
AOT build wall time also includes Clang optimization/code generation/linking.
Compiler wall observations can vary with OS caching, scheduling, and other activity; run both phases without concurrent build/test/fuzz jobs.
Code-section sizes and executable file bytes are not peak or resident process memory.
One process warmup and five samples do not control core placement, clock overhead, thermals, or background work.
A retained raw unknown-index guard may be hoisted or simplified later by LLVM; raw and optimized shapes are separate.
These observations establish neither universal speedups nor whole-language throughput rankings.
